prerequisites: Suitable knowledge of math (algebra, derivative and simple integrals)

learning_outcomes.text: Achieve the basic knowledge about the operation of fluid machines.
Achieve the basic knowledge about the configuration and the operation of steam power plants, gas turbines, combined cycles and combined heat and power systems.
Achieve the basic knowledge about the configuration and the operation of hydro power plants, photovoltaic and wind power generation systems.
Achieve the ability to calculate the performance of prime movers (turbines) or operating machines (pumps, compressors, fans).
Achieve the ability to choose the pump or the fan required by hydraulic circuits or ventilation systems.
Achieve the ability to describe the working principle and the thermodynamic cycle of steam power plants, gas turbines, combined cycles and combined heat and power systems.
Achieve the ability to evaluate the main performance (efficiency, power output and net energy production) of power generation plants or combined heat and power systems.
Achieve the ability to evaluate the main performance of hydro, photovoltaic and wind power generation plants according to the primary source availability.
Achieve the ability to evaluate the energy production cost of a power generation plant.

Achieve the ability to find technical and cost data from the equipment suppliers to perform a comparative assessment (qualitative and quantitative) between different energy power generation systems and find the most effective solution.
Achieve the ability to represent the scheme and the main transformations of fluid machines and thermodynamic cycles of power generation plants.
Achieve the ability to describe the configuration and the operation of fluid machines and power generation plants.
Achieve the ability to use the contents of other courses to enhance the knowledge in the field of fluid machines and power generation plants.

The course will also allow to consolidate the skills required by the master
’s degree courses as well as for the professional training.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and summary of Applied Thermodynamics
Classification of fluid machines and energy conversion systems
First Law of Thermodynamics, thermodynamic properties of fluids, thermodynamic diagrams and cycles
Real work, adiabatic and polytropic processes
The stage of a turbomachine: the stator and the rotor
The Euler equation and the velocity triangles
The shape of nozzles and diffusers
Choice of the operating machine in relation to the circuit
Operating machines in series and in parallel
Wind turbines: energy balance, power coefficient and power curve
Overall efficiency and specific fuel consumption of a power plant
Capacity factor and electricity production cost
Electricity market, incentives to power generation from renewable sources, CO2 emission factors
Rankine cycle, energy balance and cycle efficiency
Influence of operating parameters on the performance of a steam cycle
The main system components: steam generator, condenser, pumps, turbine and heat exchangers
Steam power plants fueled by biomass and integrated with concentrated solar collectors
Brayton cycle, energy balance and cycle efficiency
Maximum useful work and maximum efficiency
Adoption of regeneration in gas turbines
Current technologies of micro gas turbines, aeroderivative and industrial gas turbines
The basic scheme of a combined-cycle gas / steam power plant
The energy balance of the heat recovery steam generator
The combined production of electricity and heat
System configurations and performance (efficiency and primary energy saving)
Power curve of a wind turbine
assessment_rules: The final mark is reported on a 30-point basis and depends on the marks of the written test (50%) and oral examination (50%). A positive evaluation during an intermediate test will exempt students from the final written test. The minimum mark to pass the exam is 18/30. Criteria for evaluation include correctness of solution process, assumptions, calculations, answers completeness, analysis, language skills and presentation effectiveness.
